image_description:
## 1) Chart type
- **Top:** **Faceted packed-dot / bubble comparison chart** (each country-period shown as a separate dot-filled circle; dots represent counts).
- **Bottom:** **Proportional symbol map** (dot-filled circles placed on a geographic map).

## 2) Layout techniques
- **Top section:** Uses **small multiples / faceting** by country and time period. No stacking.
- **Bottom section:** Uses a **map layout** with **proportional symbols** positioned geographically by destination country.
- **Color highlighting:** Ukraine-related values are highlighted in **magenta**, while comparison cases/background symbols are **gray**.

## 3) Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Country / place name | Categorical/nominal | Facet title/label (top); map label (bottom); geographic location on map (bottom) |
| Time period / year range | Temporal | Text label under country names in top facets |
| Number of refugees / one-year increase in refugees | Quantitative | Size/area of packed-dot circle; number of dots; numeric text label |
| Individual people count unit (“each dot represents 1,000 people”) | Quantitative | Dot repetition/count within circles |
| Ukraine vs. other countries / highlighted status | Categorical/nominal | Color/hue (magenta for Ukraine-related circles, gray for others) |
| Geographic location | Spatial | Position on map (bottom panel) |

comments.raw_comment:
What do you notice? 
In the graph, I notice that there are 9 circles all ranging in sizes. From here I notice that each dot within the circles represents 1000 people, so the bigger the circle the more people, or refugees in this case. Ukraine has the second-largest amount of refugees in just the last month compared to the other countries that were totaled over the span of a year. 
What do you wonder?
I wonder if this graph is showing the direct effect that the war between Russia and Ukraine is having on the populations. To think that in less than a month over 2 million people have fled Ukraine is truly mind opening because it shows the true fear imposed in their lives over the past few weeks. I wonder what the numbers are going to look like in Ukraine in another month, and then when the war is over. 
How does this relate to you and your community?
This affects my community because the crisis that is going on in Ukraine is all over the news and on every channel so I am fully aware of what is going on at all times. Additionally, with Ukrainians seeking refugee, many are going to leave their homeland for someplace like the US, where I live. Immigration and emigration effects everyone in the world, along with me and my community. 
What's going on in this graph?
"Just how many Ukrainians are seeking refugee?"

The first thing that I noticed was the surge of Ukrainian refugees from Feb. 24 - March 13 and that the majority of them are going to Poland. The amount of refugees fleeing shows that Ukraine is getting more and more dangerous to live in by the day. The second thing that I noticed was that the amount of refugees that increased in each country was after a serious conflict or war. What struck me the most was that there was not a single country that had less than 500,000 refugees flee in under a year.

There are many things that I wonder about this graph. To begin, why are they in circles? Is it to represent the amount of people in a more concise way? Second of all, could the amount of refugees be impacted by how strict the country's borders are? What about the geographical location of each nation? 

This affects me and my community because there is a large chance that the US will see an increase in refugees coming to our borders. I think that these individuals deserve all the help they can get in order to assimilate properly into their new lives.

But, some of the best headlines will be published in Friday’s Reveal that will appear below today’s graphs and instructions.

comments.raw_comment:
What do you notice?
I notice that during each year that refugees left their countries, the time period was an era of war or disagreement between countries. As a result, refugees flee to countries that neighbor their own. When examining Ukraine’s graph, it is evident that most people fled to Poland and the least traveled to Belarus. Belarus is one of the only countries that sided with Russia. Russia may have received some Ukrainian refugees because they could have family or dual citizenship with the country.
What do you wonder?
I wonder if the remainder of people in Ukraine have access (or how do they have access) to the internet/news to know where to go or what is happening. Did they know to go to Poland because it is a NATO territory?
How does this relate to you and your community? 
This relates to our community because each country receives and aides refugees. I also believe that the US is a diverse country that houses many different cultures, beliefs, and backgrounds. Our country should be concerned with this situation to support past refugees and welcome those who still need assistance.

What do you notice?
I notice that only from February 24 to March 13 more people have fled from Ukraine than people from Afghanistan from 1980-1981. This implies that life in Ukraine right now is not safe therefore people are seeking safety by fleeing the country at very rapid rates. In the second graph, we can see that refugees from Ukraine mostly fled to Poland and Hungary. This I think is implying that these counties have safe environments and are ready to help the refugees that enter the country. 
 
What do you wonder?
What makes me wonder is the thousands of refugees that fled to Russia. My question I guess is why? However, I understand that under these impossible circumstances people are trying to find a safe place wherever they can and perhaps dual citizenship or a family present in Russia may be the case.  

How does this relate to you and your community?
This relates to me because as human beings we have to stand up for each other and do all we can to help the Ukrainian refugees with all that we can. Also if the war keeps going Russia will start drawing people from countries around such as Armenia and both my brother and father would be drawn to fight for the Russian army.

comments.raw_comment: I notice that there have been a very large amount of Ukrainian refugees in a relatively short period of time compared to other crises, and that the vast majority have chosen to flee into NATO countries such as Poland, Hungary and Slovakia. However, a sizable amount have also chosen to go into Russia. There are some points I wonder about, such as the percentage of the population that fled in the other crises pictured. I doubt places such as Venezuela and Rwanda have comparable populations to Ukraine, and I believe the percentage of population leaving would say more about the scale of the crisis than simply the amount. I also wonder about the relatively low influx of refugees into Romania compared to other NATO countries. As a student in an international school, this may affect the people I meet, but from the graph I can see that most are going to countries that border Ukraine, so it might not relate to me too much.

For older generations that have lived through similar events the massive size of what is happening should be alarming and bring back memories of previous events. I notice...
I notice that over just one month in Ukraine, there is almost the same amount of refugees as there were in an entire year in Venezuela, and there were more refugees in that one month than in a singular year in Afghanistan, Rwanda, Syria, Iraq, South Sudan, Ethiopia, and Liberia.

I wonder...
I wonder if these specific years were chosen because they were the years with the highest number of refugees for these places. I also wonder how long this may go on in Ukraine and how many people wanted to or tried to leave but were unable to. 

How does this impact our community?
This impacts our community because Florida has a very diverse population with many immigrants and chances are, we will get more immigrants, likely from Ukraine, coming to our schools and workplaces and educating us on what they have been through. Many people our age have fled Ukraine so this makes us more aware of how much we have and that we should be more grateful for our lives and how we have it easier than so many other people.
